findings: v2 main.tex:316 (the clause 'this holds when that group has no non-trivial invariant factor torus on which its linear part projects to an amenable group (Theorem 5 of bekka2015spectral)') and v2 main.tex:879 (the appendix route 'then the action of that group has a spectral gap, hence is ergodic'), v1 main.tex:818-821: Theorem 3.5 needs only the implication 'not ergodic => (ii)', which is elementary and proved here with no citation and no spectral gap (EGF.isGroupErgodic_of_not_bgConditionII): a non-trivial invariant set gives an invariant indicator with a non-zero Fourier frequency k; the moduli of the coefficients are constant along k -> B^T k (B a linear part), so by Parseval this orbit is finite; its annihilator W is a proper rational subspace invariant under the linear parts, and their projections on Q^d/W are determined by maps of the finite orbit, so they form a finite, hence amenable, group: (ii) holds. Bekka-Guivarc'h's Theorem 5 (the hard direction (i) => (ii), spectral gap) is not needed for Theorem 3.5; it is needed only if the paper wants the spectral gap itself. So EGF.universality_tori's hypothesis BekkaGuivarchTheorem5 d is redundant (EGF.universality_tori_of_not_bgConditionII). The author may want v2 l.879 to say 'If condition (ii) is false ..., the group acts ergodically: an invariant set A would give an invariant indicator whose non-zero Fourier frequencies have finite orbits under the transposed linear parts, and the annihilator of such an orbit is an invariant factor torus with finite (hence amenable) projection', keeping the spectral-gap remark as context. Proposed for C-28's batch (or a new entry); not a reading.

v2 main.tex:316, the e.g.: T(STS^-1)^-1 = [[2,1],[1,1]] checked as a matrix identity (EGF.matT_mul_inv_conj) and, for every choice of the four translations, Phi_T (Phi_S Phi_T Phi_S^-1)^-1 lies in the group of the minimal four moves with that linear part (EGF.minimalMoves_example_of_record). Confirmation, no correction.

C-54 (found): its strongest form is proved for both theorems (both hypotheses at one parameter, for any family containing the model's flows there), and 'the flows of the family at these translation parts are then EGFs' is proved in a stronger form: every member of the family whose policy is sum_i alpha^i delta_{Phi_i} on the moves at that parameter is an EGF (EGF.universality_tori_of_record, third conjunct), in particular the flows of an affine toroidal model at every theta with M.b theta = b (EGF.universality_tori_of_record_model).

C-56 (v2 main.tex:758 and the 'p = 4 ... the two generators and their inverse' of v2 l.320): on T^2 the two moves S, T without their inverses suffice, for every choice of the translations (EGF.universality_tori_two_moves, non-vacuous by EGF.universality_tori_two_moves_l2), the members on these moves being EGFs; on T^1 one irrational translation (EGF.universality_tori_one_sqrt_two); on T^d, d >= 2, one move (EGF.exists_universality_tori_single_move, cited).
questions: v2 l.316 'a universal EGF family': read as epsilon-universal (DEC-141) together with C-54's precision (the family contains EGFs of the moves at the parameter of the hypotheses, and its members on these moves are EGFs); 'every member of the family is an EGF' is not claimed (false in general: members at other translation parts need not generate an ergodic group, C-54 finding 1).

v2 l.316 'a translation of infinite order': read as an element h of the group with coe h = (x -> x + c) and orderOf h = 0; it is equivalent to addOrderOf c = 0 (EGF.orderOf_eq_addOrderOf_of_translation), so the reading does not matter.
